beats: Your oven's bottom heater is hiding right under the floor.
Older ovens showed a bare coil down there. Newer ones tuck it underneath.
It's a steel tube with a thin resistance wire packed in mineral powder.
Current heats the wire. The powder lets heat out, but never the electricity.
The tube sits just under the oven floor: steel, coated in glossy enamel.
The floor soaks up that heat, then radiates it upward, like a baking stone.
Air touching the hot floor warms, rises, and rolls around the whole oven.
That steel is a buffer: preheat takes a little longer, but heat spreads more evenly.
Spills land on smooth enamel instead of burning onto the coil. One wipe.
When the hidden heater dies, the floor still looks spotless.
But pies come out golden on top and pale, soggy underneath.
So your oven floor isn't just a floor. It's the heater's lid.
